subject: BridgePay PO acceptance window / staggered invoice cycle
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@bridgepay.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PO requirements & invoice cadence for Redwood pilot

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — BridgePay is excited about the latency/cost profile you showed for the dedicated inference lanes. Procurement asked me to loop them in on two requirements before we can issue a formal PO:

- PO acceptance window: our AP team requires a 90-day acceptance window for initial POs on new vendors.
- Invoice cadence: our default is monthly invoices, but accounting prefers a staggered approach that aligns with milestone delivery.
- Net terms: standard is Net-60; exceptions require VP Finance approval.

I attached our PO template (BridgePay_PO_Template.pdf). Can Redwood work with these constraints? If not, what exceptions can you offer (discounts, holdbacks, acceptance criteria)?

Appreciate a quick note — procurement hopes to get the PO processed this week if possible.

Best,
Alex Johnson
Sr. Procurement Manager
BridgePay

Attachments: BridgePay_PO_Template.pdf

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@bridgepay.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements & invoice cadence for Redwood pilot

Alex — thanks for the details and the template. Quick read-through and initial thoughts below. Looping Vanessa (Head of Accounts) and Ben (Sales Ops) to weigh in on the financial/ops side.

Short answer: we can be flexible but need to align on three levers to make it work without introducing material risk for Redwood:

1) Acceptance window: 90 days is longer than our standard 30-day acceptance for initial POs. We can accept 60 days as a compromise, or take 90 days with a 10% holdback released on final acceptance.

2) Invoice cadence: monthly invoices are fine. For milestone-aligned invoicing, we can do a staggered invoice cycle provided each invoice references the PO line items and the schedule. We prefer no more than 4 invoices monthly per PO (to keep billing reconciliation tractable).

3) Net terms: Net-60 is standard market practice. We can offer Net-60 on a committed volume tier (e.g., 6+ month commit) or Net-45 with a small percentage discount if BridgePay signs a 12-month commit.

Before I draft language, quick ask: can you confirm whether BridgePay requires the 90-day acceptance and Net-60 as must-haves from Finance, or if there is flexibility? If Finance needs the 90/60 as non-negotiable, we’ll propose the holdback + small discount to bridge the economics.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed clause for the PO that we can put into a DocuSign once we agree the contours.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@bridgepay.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements & invoice cadence for Redwood pilot

Hi Vivek — appreciate the fast reply.

I checked with Finance & AP: the 90-day acceptance is their preferred baseline for new vendors (to allow product validation and security sign-off). Net-60 is the standard; Net-45 would need VP Finance sign-off which is unlikely for a new vendor.

On the invoice cadence: monthly invoices are fine; they would like the invoices to map to PO line numbers and show delivered usage (token/compute) where applicable. BridgePay is open to a small holdback if that is Redwood's standard practice for extended acceptance windows.

If you can send a short addendum or redline to the PO template that outlines the holdback mechanics and the invoice mapping, Procurement will route it through legal.

Thanks,
Alex

Procurement Ops contact: procure@bridgepay.com

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@bridgepay.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed compromise: PO acceptance / staggered invoice plan

Hi Alex — thanks for confirming Finance's position. Based on the constraints, Redwood can accept the 90-day acceptance window provided the following commercial guardrails are included in the PO/addendum:

- Holdback: 10% retention applied to the total invoice value for the first two invoice cycles following PO activation. Holdback released upon final acceptance or at day 120, whichever comes first.
- Invoice mapping: each invoice must reference the BridgePay PO number and the Redwood line items; usage details (hours / token units) included as an annex for transparency.
- Invoice frequency cap: monthly invoicing only, with a 1x mid-month adjustment allowed for true-up; cap of 2 invoices per calendar month unless mutually agreed.
- Net terms: Net-60 standard. Redwood will provide a 2% prompt-pay discount if BridgePay approves Net-45 within 30 days of initial PO activation (requires finance approval on both sides).

We attached our internal billing playbook (Redwood_Split-Invoice_Guide.pdf) that explains the holdback/release mechanics and sample invoice layout. If this sounds reasonable, Vivek / Ben and I can provide a one-paragraph PO addendum and route to legal & DocuSign.

Quick confirmation on implementation: who will be the signatory and which HubSpot deal record should we reference? I'll include the HubSpot ID in the DocuSign envelope so accounting can match records.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Accounts Receivable
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Split-Invoice_Guide.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@bridgepay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed compromise: PO acceptance / staggered invoice plan

Vanessa — this looks good and addresses most of Finance's concerns. Procurement confirmed they will accept the 10% holdback and the invoice mapping as long as the PO addendum is explicit about release triggers.

Signatory will be Melissa Hart, VP Finance (melissa.h@bridgepay.com). HubSpot deal ID is DP-9876 — please put that on the DocuSign.

Next steps: can you send the one-paragraph addendum and the DocuSign link today? We want to get the PO issued before Friday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to loop legal if needed.

Best,
Alex
